tensor_inventory_and_mapping.interpretation: The antirez GGUF is not the same artifact shape as the official DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark safetensors inference module. It is a supplementary one-layer MTP support model that relies on target embed/output and its own e_proj/h_proj path.

minimum_correct_flow: Run the accepted target model for one committed token and capture target HC state needed by MTP without changing target logits.
Run supplementary MTP in shadow mode from the accepted target token/state to draft a short greedy suffix.
Run target verification over the drafted suffix using an isolated KV/cache branch or restorable checkpoint.
Compare target top1 at each drafted position against the draft token and accept only the longest matching prefix.
Commit exactly the target KV/cache state for the accepted prefix and discard/rewind rejected suffix state.
Emit only target-verified tokens, never unverified MTP tokens.
state_requirements: MTP needs a separate raw cache because it evaluates speculative future tokens.
Target KV/cache must not be contaminated by rejected speculative rows.
DeepSeek4 compression/indexer frontiers and raw ring positions must be restored exactly on partial accept or reject.
Existing llama-lookahead failure means generic llama_memory_seq_cp/rm is not enough evidence; DeepSeek4-specific cache state must be verified.
verifier_design.cost_requirement: The verifier must batch target work sublinearly. Antirez source comments indicate an exact N=2 target verifier, and README says current MTP gives only slight speedup. Therefore an initial vendor implementation must not assume A=5 or A=7 acceptance; it must first measure N=2 correctness and cost as a diagnostic.

first_safe_runtime_probe_if_later_allowe.behavior: load supplementary MTP, capture target state, compute draft logits, but emit target-only tokens and do not change target KV/cache commits
must_pass_before_verifier: TTFT recorded and marked rejected if above gate

current_decision.reason: Tensor mapping is now mostly understood, but verifier semantics and target batch cost remain unproven. The reference implementation itself documents only slight speedup, so this is not yet a credible 10 tok/s implementation route.
current_decision.next_required_question: Could an exact N=2 verifier, implemented in vendor with strict cache rollback, beat 4.4 tok/s and approach the 10 tok/s bound under 16GB RAM and TTFT gates? If the N=2 upper bound is far below 10, do not implement MTP.
